top_story.headline: Rep. Dan Crenshaw still has no 2025 annual financial disclosure on file, 83 days past his final extension
top_story.dek: The House Clerk's index shows an extension filed June 4 and nothing since the August 13 final extension date.
paragraphs: Rep. Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-2) is the only sitting member of Congress this edition's check found with no calendar-year 2025 annual financial disclosure on file past every extension. He filed an extension on 6/4/2026. The final extension date was 8/13/2026, so the report is now 83 days overdue.

The check ran against every sitting member's filings in the Clerk of the House index and Senate eFD. The Senate half of the check failed today, so the result is only a partial check. A filing under an unexpected spelling of his name could also read as missing, so treat the finding as unconfirmed until the index is checked by hand.

Nothing else in today's input stands out. The three House filings are routine, and the foreign-agent filings are informational materials and supplemental statements. The three LDA filings that name President Donald Trump only mention him in describing legislation or an executive order.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.

sections.headline: Rep. Julie Johnson filed 8 trade reports last year, none in 91 days
paragraphs: 1 House member(s) with a history of frequent stock trading have stopped filing trade reports.

items: Rep. Julie Johnson (D-TX-32) filed 8 periodic transaction reports in the 12 months from 8/6/2025 to 8/6/2026, and none in the 91 days since the last, on 8/5/2026

blocks.text: House members who filed 6 or more periodic transaction reports (STOCK Act trade disclosures) in the year before the last 90 days and none since, per the House Clerk's disclosure index. Silence doesn't say why: the member may have sold off holdings, moved assets into a blind trust or index fund, been covered by a new law, or just not traded -- and trades are reportable up to 45 days late, so the latest ones may not be filed yet. House members only; the Senate's e-filing search isn't covered.
